verdict: Arm posted a record $1.24B quarter, up 26%, with royalties hitting a record $737M — but GAAP net income slipped 12% to $223M because last year's investment gains did not repeat, even as operating income rose.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: vs a year ago; a record quarter

kpis.label: Free cash flow
kpis.note: non-GAAP, down 52% YoY; operating cash flow was $365M

segments.name: License and other revenue
segments.note: Fees for licensing Arm chip designs, plus support and related services; up 25% YoY on the timing and size of high-value license agreements and contributions from backlog.

segments.name: Royalty revenue
segments.note: A cut of every chip shipped with Arm technology inside; up 27% YoY on higher royalty rates from newer designs such as Armv9 and Arm CSS, and more Arm-based chips in data centers.

opex.name: Research and development
opex.note: Designing new processors and platform technology; the GAAP figure includes $204M of share-based pay (paying staff in shares) and $21M of related employer taxes.

opex.name: Selling, general and administrative
opex.note: Selling and running the company; the GAAP figure includes $73M of share-based pay and $6M of related employer taxes.

opex.name: Disposal, restructuring and other
opex.note: One-off disposal and restructuring costs — excluded from Arm's non-GAAP results.

follow100Note: Royalties alone are $59.34 of every $100 Arm takes in. Tax took just $0.40 of every $100 this quarter. The rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
otherDetail: Combined other income was $43M: $29M of net interest income and $8M of other non-operating income, plus $6M of income from equity investments (the separate equity line). Tax was a $5M charge, a 2.2% effective rate on $228M of pre-tax income.
footerNote: Arm calls its direct cost 'cost of sales' ($30M). Tax was only a $5M charge this quarter, versus a $16M charge a year ago.

takeaways.title: Royalties set another record
takeaways.text: Royalty revenue rose 27% to a record $737M and license revenue 25% to $505M, taking total revenue to a record $1,242M — Arm's fourth straight billion-dollar quarter. Data center royalties grew by triple digits as Arm-based server chips spread.

takeaways.title: GAAP profit is much smaller than the headline
takeaways.text: GAAP EPS was $0.21 while non-GAAP EPS was $0.43. The gap is mostly $285M of share-based pay plus $28M of related employer taxes — and equity investments added only $6M this quarter, versus $39M a year ago, which is why GAAP net income fell 12% even as operating income rose 6%.

takeaways.title: The license pipeline keeps building
takeaways.text: Annualized contract value (ACV) — a normalized view of license revenue — rose 28% to $1,620M, and customers have now signed 21 Compute Subsystems (CSS) licenses. For Q4 FY26 Arm guided revenue to about $1.47B (plus or minus $50M).

oneTimers: Share-based pay is the main gap between the two profit numbers: the non-GAAP reconciliation adds back $285M of equity-settled share-based compensation (including $8M in cost of sales) plus $28M of related employer taxes (net of R&D incentives) and $6M of restructuring costs, which is why GAAP net income of $223M sits far below non-GAAP net income of $457M.
Net income got only a $6M lift from equity investments this quarter, versus $39M a year ago — that swing, not the core business, is why GAAP profit fell year on year.
